claims.text: Atomic-scale lattice distortions enhance the dynamic mechanical behavior of high-entropy alloys.
Atomic-scale lattice distortions delay dislocation nucleation in high-entropy alloys.
Atomic-scale lattice distortions promote activation of multiple slip systems in high-entropy alloys.
Delayed dislocation nucleation and activation of multiple slip systems enable high strength and ductility during dynamic loading.
The proposed initial HEA is homogeneous and single-phase.
The proposed initial HEA has significant chemical complexity and inherent lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions and chemically induced heterogeneities alter dislocation behavior.
Diverse atomic environments in HEAs create local strain fields.
The local strain fields interact with dislocations and delay their nucleation.
The local strain fields encourage activation of multiple slip systems.
Delayed dislocation nucleation and multiple-slip activation produce more spatially distributed plastic deformation.
Under identical dynamic testing, the HEA will have higher yield strength than the conventional-alloy baseline.
Under identical dynamic testing, the HEA will exhibit a more gradual onset of plastic flow than the conventional-alloy baseline.
The dynamically tested HEA will exhibit a heterogeneous dislocation network.
The dynamically tested HEA will show evidence of multiple active slip systems.
The baseline conventional alloy has lower configurational entropy and limited lattice distortion.
The proposed mechanism should apply to HEAs with appreciable lattice distortion under dynamic loading.
At extreme temperatures or under static loading, deformation mechanisms other than the proposed mechanism may dominate.
